text.p: Giordano International Ltd said on Monday it was addressing regulatory demands concerning its operations in China and was seeking investors to raise its profile there and in other markets.
The retailer said in a statement that negotiations relating to the setting up of new Giordano retail outlets in Beijing and Shanghai had not been concluded.

"The company is concurrently in active negotiations with certain other Chinese enterprises who have approached the directors for joint-venture arrangements for all or some of the group's China operations," it said.

"Whilst the group's operations in China have in the recent past encountered inconveniences resulting from regulatory procedural requirements and have received demands for levies and other payments, the directors are continuing with their efforts to achieve an acceptable resolution of these demands and requirements," Giordano added.
It said the total amount of these demands would not seriously affect the financial stability of the group.
Trading in Giordano shares has been suspended since January 17 and the company said it has requested that trading resume on Monday. The stock last traded at HK$5.05.
